standard.title: Methods of Test for Determination of Flammability of Solid Electrical Insulating Materials When Exposed to an Igniting Source (ठोस विद्युत रोधी सामग्रियों के ज्वलनशीलता निर्धारण के लिए परीक्षण विधियाँ जब एक प्रज्वलन स्रोत के संपर्क में लाया जाए)
standard.sector: Electrotechnical / Solid Electrical Insulating Materials and Insulation Systems

sectional_committee.name: Solid Electrical Insulating Materials and Insulation Systems Sectional Committee

standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes two testing orientations (horizontal and vertical) to evaluate and classify the ignitability, flame propagation speed, and self-extinguishing characteristics of solid polymer and resin-based electrical insulating materials when exposed to a standardized open flame igniting source.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes two testing orientations (horizontal and vertical) to evaluate and classify the ignitability, flame propagation speed, and self-extinguishing characteristics of solid polymer and resin-based electrical insulating materials when exposed to a standardized open flame igniting source.

supersedes: None (Developed as the primary Indian Standard methods for testing non-metallic solid electrical flammability)

certification.description: Mandatory Testing Compliance. Under municipal utilities, public works specifications, and smart meter box mandates, raw polymers and terminal moldings must be certified to comply with IS 11731 (Part 2) Class FV0.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, burning times, or specimen dimensions must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
Specimens must be rectangular bars measuring 125 ± 5 mm in length, 13.0 ± 0.3 mm in width, and 3.0 ± 0.2 mm in thickness.
Two lines are scribed across the specimen at 25 mm and 100 mm from the free end to calculate exact linear burning rates.
The standardized 20 mm blue Bunsen flame is applied horizontally to the free end of the specimen for exactly 30 seconds or until the flame front reaches the first mark.
FH1 indicates a burn rate of <= 40 mm/min for specimens >= 3 mm thick. FH2 indicates a burn rate of <= 75 mm/min for thin specimens (< 3 mm) or self-extinguishing behavior.
Specimens are identical rectangular bars clamped vertically. A cotton indicator pad is placed horizontally exactly 300 mm below the specimen lower end.
A 20 mm flame is applied directly underneath the vertically clamped bar for 10 seconds. Afterflame is recorded. The flame is applied for another 10 seconds immediately after self-extinguishing.
Afterflame time per burn <= 10 seconds; total afterflame time of 5 specimens (10 burns) <= 50 seconds; zero flaming drips (no cotton pad ignition).
Afterflame time per burn <= 30 seconds; total afterflame time of 5 specimens <= 250 seconds; zero flaming drips; glowing ceases within 60 seconds.
Afterflame time per burn <= 30 seconds; total afterflame time of 5 specimens <= 250 seconds; flaming drips are permitted to ignite the cotton indicator pad.
